candidates.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
candidates.author: OpenAI (no byline)
candidates.what_changed: OpenAI disclosed its layered anti-distillation stack and hardened protected-reasoning (chain-of-thought) extraction defenses in GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol; API now ties protected reasoning to the conversation history that produced it and drops it if an earlier message is rewritten; older model families can no longer read GPT-6.2 encrypted reasoning.
candidates.mechanism: Request level: adversarial training on harvested successful attacks, input classifiers for extraction attempts, output classifiers on assistant messages AND tool-call arguments (streaming and non-streaming), API controls on reuse of encrypted reasoning across user/workspace/org/model-family boundaries. Campaign level: account/request signal correlation, network-wide enforcement, sharing IOCs with other providers; attacks found feed back into training and regression tests.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor-measured internal evals (adaptive black-box red-teaming across six attacker models); no external replication.
candidates.relevance: High for platform/security teams: tool-call arguments as a leak channel, keeping successful attacks as regression tests, binding reasoning state to conversation history. Also an API behavior change for anyone replaying/editing conversation history with reasoning models.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Related to prior-edition OpenAI safety posts (managing-frontier-ai-risk, GPT-6.2 launch) but this URL is new.
candidates.summary: Adaptive black-box extraction attack success rate: extracting protected reasoning from an earlier request fell from 54.0% (GPT-6 Astra, original safeguards) to 0.2% (GPT-6.2 Astra, updated); from the current request 22.9% -> 0.9%. Selected improvements being back-ported to GPT-6 Astra. Internal cyber-distillation study: same pretrained student SFT'd on Astra-level teacher trajectories (coding + defensive cyber); student trained on exact reasoning traces generally beat the one trained on reasoning summaries after SFT; after light RL the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget, summary-trained student higher at lower budgets (footnote cites similar Anthropic SWE-bench Verified finding). Weekly enforcement actions ranged from thousands to tens of thousands of accounts, rate up significantly in summer 2026. Attributes a September campaign partly to individuals associated with Moonshot AI (Kimi); February congressional briefing on DeepSeek. Supports Chip Security Act, AI OVERWATCH Act, MATCH Act. Recommendations for other developers: check assistant messages and tool-call args for leaks, restrict encrypted-reasoning reuse, keep extraction attacks as regression tests and replay them plus adaptive red-teaming, combine request-level and campaign-level defenses, coordinate with deployment partners.

candidates.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
candidates.author: Jakub Pachocki (Chief Scientist, OpenAI)
candidates.pub_date: 2026-11-22 (RSS pubDate 00:00 GMT date-only; page shows November 22, 2026)
candidates.what_changed: OpenAI published, for the first time, internal pretraining log-perplexity numbers on its held-out (internal codebase) eval set and proposed perplexity/cross-entropy as a cross-lab shared metric for safety standards.
candidates.mechanism: Track log-perplexity on a fixed held-out dataset as a measure of the pretraining 'intelligence substrate', independent of downstream benchmarks that saturate.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor disclosure of internal measurements; opinion/position piece. No independent confirmation; numbers not comparable across labs (author concedes).
candidates.relevance: Medium: evals/measurement framing; useful context for how labs gauge progress and for eval-awareness concerns. Not directly actionable for practitioners.
candidates.summary: Log-perplexity on OpenAI's main internal-codebase eval set: GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91; models started producing 'groundbreaking' math results at ~0.76; author expects further transformative capabilities in the ~0.68-0.70 window, along with degradation of current alignment auditing and more evaluation/training awareness. Footnote: steep loss acceleration in 2026 attributed mostly to long-term research and compute investment, smaller part to automation, with 'meaningful design contributions coming from AI' in recent models. Listed challenges: cross-lab comparability (different datasets/mixtures), detachment from actionable tasks, ignores post-pretraining gains like chain-of-thought, unknown entropy floor. Calls for industry transparency on perplexity.

candidates.title: How to build a knowledge factory
candidates.author: Harrison Chase
candidates.what_changed: LangChain framed a 'knowledge factory' pattern it runs internally (GTM and content-studio agents; LangSmith Engine keeps one per agent).
candidates.mechanism: Separate context (what an agent has for a task) from knowledge (reusable understanding). Three knowledge types: skills (procedures), domain knowledge (slow-changing facts/definitions), data-access guidance (what lives where, how to query; don't copy source-of-truth data). Factory parts: a tool for working agents to flag missing/wrong knowledge (and optionally suggest fixes); a separate curator agent (runs e.g. nightly) that reviews flags and traces and updates knowledge, rather than letting task agents edit it; storage-agnostic (skills in GitHub, Notion, OKF in LangSmith Context Hub, Neo4j).
candidates.evidence_quality: Opinion/experience post; no metrics.
candidates.relevance: High: concrete, applicable memory/context-maintenance pattern for agent teams; ties to prior issues' agent memory themes.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Same author/series as prior-edition LangChain posts (from-tasks-to-goals, proactive agents); new topic.
candidates.summary: Worked example: revenue-report agent uses BigQuery/Salesforce raw data (context) plus skills (report style, GitHub), long-lived knowledge (ARR definition, wiki), data-access skills (Context Hub). Agent notices a renamed BigQuery column, works around it, and flags it via a report-issue tool; finance lead corrects header formatting in-session. That night the curator agent reads the flag and the trace of the back-and-forth and updates both skills. Argument: letting task agents maintain knowledge makes it 'unruly and full of contradictions'. Advice: start with one recurring workflow, see where agents struggle, close the loop. Ends with a sales pitch to work with customers.

candidates.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
candidates.author: Younes Belkada, Ben Burtenshaw, Nathan Habib, Lysandre Debut, Amine Dirhoussi, Adithya S K, Shaun Smith, Sergio Paniego, Joel Niklaus, Lewis Tunstall et al.
candidates.what_changed: Released per-harness RL-trained LoRA adapters for Qwen3.8-27B (pi, Hermes Agent, OpenCode), a merged 'super-adapter', an 871-task agentic-coding RL dataset, and a reproducible recipe on HF Jobs.
candidates.mechanism: RL (TRL AsyncGRPOTrainer) inside the unmodified harness via OpenEnv/Harbor; a proxy between harness and vLLM records exact tokens. Task pipeline: SWE-smith + SWE-Gym (TaskTrove) + Tasksmith (tasks from merged PRs), metadata/decontam screen, openenv validate semantic checks (oracle max, floor gap, canary floor, determinism), difficulty filter keeping tasks base model solves only sometimes. Reward = verifier pass/fail + 0.1 tool-efficiency bonus. LoRA merge by rank concatenation at weight 1/2.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor-measured, artifacts and data released (reproducible); small eval sets (50-51 SWE-bench Pro hard, 82-89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks), single attempt per task.
candidates.relevance: High: practical recipe for adapting open models to your own agent harness for accuracy and token cost; verifier-validation lessons apply to anyone building RL envs or evals.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Prior edition had other HF posts (MoE streaming, fine-tuning time) but not this.
candidates.summary: Headline: Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 2.1 in pi harness 39% at ~2.9K tokens/task -> 55% pass@1 at ~1.5K tokens with a harness LoRA (less reasoning, fewer tool calls). SWE-bench Pro hard (51), pi: base 40.0% -> pi-adapted 64.0% (with ~60% efficiency gain); hermes: 29.4% -> 43.1%; super-adapter 47.1% under hermes. Task funnel: ~59,000 Harbor tasks found on Hub; 858 of 1,127 Hub candidates passed validation; of 442 scored tasks, base solved 151 always, 120 never, 171 sometimes (qualified). Validation caught a Tasksmith task accepting incomplete implementations and a Terminal-Bench 2.1 verifier (regex-log) accepting known-wrong answers. Dataset harness-hub/agentic-coding-envs: 871 tasks from 35 repos (SWE-smith 717/144 qualified, SWE-Gym 130/27, Tasksmith 24/22). LR sweep: 1e-5 no movement, 1e-4 collapsed rollouts (18->6 turns), 5e-5 improved 0.49->0.60 but unstable longer; final 2e-5. Training on 2xB200 per adapter (1 vLLM, 1 trainer). Adapter updates nearly orthogonal (cosine 0.01-0.02). Merge weights on 89 TB2.1 tasks: base 43.3% avg / 49.2 tool calls; 1/3 49.2% / 35.6; 1/2 52.5% / 25.9; sum 50.0% / 13.4 (hermes 62.8% but pi back to base).

candidates.organization: Hugging Face (model by Thinking Machines Lab)
candidates.what_changed: Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini open model, with day-0 transformers, llama.cpp, MLX and SGLang support.

candidates.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
candidates.author: AWS (authors listed on page)
candidates.what_changed: New agent skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS (works with Kiro, Claude Code) that evaluates, sets up and troubleshoots distributed L2 KV caching (LMCache + ElastiCache for Valkey over EFA RDMA) for self-hosted vLLM/SGLang; plus KVTrace tool to estimate savings from your own traffic.
candidates.mechanism: Skill walks agent through: read-only fit check (describe-instances, EFA count), asks engine/model/TP/KV dtype/price/repeat rate; checks cheaper fixes first (re-enable prefix caching, session affinity); KVTrace records KV cache events (block hashes and token counts only, no prompt text) and replays offline against candidate cache sizes, recommending smallest capacity reaching 90% of savings ceiling; computes prefill-vs-load cutover prompt length; setup aligns KV ID mechanism (hash+seed) and KV dtype across servers; pre-prod check that two cache-loaded runs give identical output (layout mismatch can yield healthy hit counters but wrong answers); explicit approval before resource changes.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor claim ('up to 40%' cost, 'up to 80%' TTFT) from linked benchmarks; no independent confirmation.
candidates.relevance: High: cost/latency ops for self-hosted inference, and a good example of packaging ops runbooks as agent skills with approval gates.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Related to prior AWS KV-cache-aware routing and NVIDIA Dynamo items; distinct post.
candidates.summary: Example: legal assistant with 64K-token contexts on p5 had 13 s TTFT on returning conversations due to cold prefill. Sizing example: 8 p5 instances serving 64K prompts -> agent recommends two cache.i8ge.48xlarge nodes. Prereqs: EFA RDMA-write GPUs (p5), LMCache >=0.5.8rc1, vLLM >=0.11.1 or SGLang >=0.5.13, ElastiCache for Valkey >=9.1. Troubleshooting flow diagnoses rdma_write_errors as a security group blocking intra-group EFA traffic.

candidates.title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
candidates.author: Daniele Molteni, Pawel Klimek, Denzil Correa
candidates.what_changed: WAF rules (Free and Managed rulesets, Block default) for a critical Ruby heap overflow reachable pre-auth in default Rails and classic Sinatra apps.
candidates.mechanism: Upcasing German sharp s (one byte -> 'SS') in 14 single-byte ISO-8859/Windows-125x encodings writes two bytes with room checked for one; 21 sharp-s chars overflow by one byte; reached via upcase, swapcase, downcase(:fold), casecmp?; UTF-8 unaffected.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor writeup citing Ruby advisory and Veria Labs research.
candidates.relevance: Low for AI focus; general security ops (patch Ruby 3.3.14/3.4.13/4.0.10). Better fit for slice D security if covered.
candidates.summary: Bundled-Ruby products affected at disclosure include GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, OpenProject, Discourse, Chatwoot. Second rule covers related GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px. Veria Labs PoC expected ~a week after disclosure.

candidates.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
candidates.author: Daniele Molteni, Kuber Nandwani, Christian Larsen
candidates.what_changed: WAF coverage for phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714, CVSS 4.0 9.2) and three new Managed rules for PHP-FPM smuggling and SOAP flaws.
candidates.mechanism: Interrupted write of file-based session leaves mixed new/old serialized data; next session_start() deserializes attacker-controlled objects; session upload progress one way to plant data.
candidates.evidence_quality: Vendor writeup citing PHP advisory/depthfirst.
candidates.relevance: Low for AI focus; security ops. Better fit for slice D.
candidates.summary: Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0 along with 16 other vulns. Existing php2shell RCE rule (Oct 2026) already partly detected pattern; updated Nov 19. New rules default to Log. No known exploitation as of Nov 19 (none in CISA KEV).
